title: Abelian sheaf cohomology vanishes on profinite topological spaces
statement: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological space (a profinite space). For every abelian sheaf $G$ on the site of open subsets of $X$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and every integer $q>0$, $H^q(X,G)=0$, where cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].

proof.text: Let $\varphi:F\to E$ be an epimorphism of abelian sheaves on $X$ and $e\in E(X)$. By [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-epi-iff-stalk-epi], for each $x\in X$ choose a germ $a_x\in F_x$ with $\varphi_x(a_x)=e_x$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] to abelian presheaves as modules over the constant presheaf $\mathbf Z$: represent $a_x$ by $f_x\in F(V_x)$; equality of the image germ and $e_x$ gives an open $x\in U_x\subseteq V_x$ on which $\varphi(f_x|_{U_x})=e|_{U_x}$. Thus the opens $U_x$ cover $X$ with lifts of $e$.

source.place: Tag 0A3F (lemma-vanishing-for-profinite), local section lifts; Sheaves Section 0078 (section-stalks), equality of germs

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis], for each $x$ choose a clopen $C_x$ with $x\in C_x\subseteq U_x$. Compactness of $X$ supplies a finite subcover $C_1,\ldots,C_n$. Put $D_1=C_1$ and $D_i=C_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}C_j$ for $2\leq i\leq n$. A finite union of clopens is clopen, so each $D_i$ is clopen; the $D_i$ are pairwise disjoint, cover $X$, and $D_i\subseteq C_i\subseteq U_{x_i}$. Discard empty parts. If $X=\varnothing$, take the empty cover. This proves the finite disjoint refinement used in Topology Tag 08ZZ directly from the cited basis and compactness.

source.place: Tag 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering); elementary finite refinement from its clopen basis consequence

proof.text: Restrict the chosen lift on $U_{x_i}$ to $D_i$. These sections agree on pairwise intersections: distinct parts have empty intersection, and the sheaf axiom for the empty cover says $F(\varnothing)=0$. The equalizer sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] glues them to $f\in F(X)$. Naturality gives $\varphi(f)|_{D_i}=e|_{D_i}$, and uniqueness in the sheaf axiom gives $\varphi(f)=e$. Hence every epimorphism of abelian sheaves induces a surjection on global sections, including when $X$ is empty. Together with the additivity and left exactness of $\Gamma(X,-)$ stated in that node, global sections are exact.

source.place: Tag 0A3F (lemma-vanishing-for-profinite), surjectivity and exactness of global sections

proof.text: To spell out the higher-derived-functor vanishing rather than invoke it without a citation, use [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] on the site of opens of $X$. Fix a Grothendieck universe containing $X$, and take covering families indexed by sets in this universe; the opens, inclusions and covering families then form sets in a larger universe. The site axioms hold: the identity covers its target, a composite of open covers covers its target, and pulling back an open cover along an inclusion gives the cover by intersections. This restriction of index sets gives exactly the usual sheaves: after deleting repetitions any open cover is indexed by a subset of the set of opens of $X$, and matching sections at repeated copies of the same open must be equal on that open. Thus the sheaf axiom for the bounded families implies it for every open cover. For any abelian sheaf $G$, choose a monomorphism $G\hookrightarrow I$ with $I$ injective and let $Q$ be its cokernel. In the abelian category this yields a short exact sequence $0\to G\to I\to Q\to0$: [def-sp-abelian] says every monomorphism is a kernel, if the embedding $i$ is $\ker(h)$, then $h$ factors through $c=\operatorname{coker}(i)$. Any map killed by $c$ is killed by $h$, hence factors uniquely through $i$; conversely $ci=0$. Thus $i=\ker(c)$, giving the condition in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The identifications $H^0(X,A)=A(X)$ and $H^r(X,I)=0$ for $r>0$ are provided by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 01DZ (section-cohomology-sheaves); Tag 0A3F, final sentence expanded; Derived Categories Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), injective vanishing

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] to $\Gamma(X,-)$, which is additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and whose source has enough injectives as in Step 4. The long exact sequence contains $I(X)\to Q(X)\to H^1(X,G)\to H^1(X,I)=0$. Step 3 makes its first map surjective, since $I\to Q$ is an epimorphism. Exactness therefore makes the connecting map zero and also surjective, so $H^1(X,G)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $G$.

source.place: Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), long exact sequence; details of Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor) used in Cohomology Tag 0A3F

proof.text: Induct on the positive degree, with the claim for all abelian sheaves simultaneously. Step 5 is the base degree $1$. Suppose $H^r(X,A)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $A$, where $r\geq1$, and apply the sequence of Step 4 to any $G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] the segment $H^r(X,I)\to H^r(X,Q)\to H^{r+1}(X,G)\to H^{r+1}(X,I)$ is exact. The two terms for $I$ vanish by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and the term for $Q$ vanishes by the induction hypothesis. Thus $H^{r+1}(X,G)=0$. This proves the claim for every integer $q>0$ with precisely the cohomology of [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].
